text:
maya: Heads-up: console shows a noticeable latency + token-accounting delta between v1 and v2 for cohort 'shadow-A'. Anyone else tracking this?
liam: I saw a blip earlier. What's the magnitude?
maya: v1 p95 ~120ms, v2 p95 ~210ms for short responses (<100 tokens). Token tally for the same requests is ~12% higher on v2.
cheng: can you paste the console query or a snippet of the timeline? might be aggregation difference (per-route vs per-variant).
maya: pasted the console query snapshot: `SELECT route, variant, p95_latency_ms, tokens FROM metrics WHERE cohort='shadow-A' AND ts>now()-1h`
maya: result snippet: v1 p95 118ms tokens 9.8k; v2 p95 212ms tokens 11.0k
hailey: two quick suspects: micro-batching in v2 increasing tail for short seqs, and a billing pipeline header change that could affect token dedupe.
liam: micro-batching would push up p95 for small workloads; kv-cache eviction behavior could also cause higher latency.
maya: @liam @cheng can we check routing logs? I'm seeing both base-v2 and base-v2-quantized in the same minute.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout event logged: console.flag.v2_rollout toggle=on for tenant shadow-A at 2025-03-05T14:02:10Z
cheng: rollouts toggled earlier today. If fallbacks prefer quantized variants under different load thresholds, that could change observed latency.
hailey: telemetry note: billing pipeline deduped tokens differently for v2 for a while due to an `x-variant` -> `x-model-variant` header rename. that explains the 12% accounting bump.
maya: billing bump explainable, but why p95 doubled? we need an isolation plan.
liam: propose a 2-hour A/B: pin traffic to v1 vs pin to v2 on the same hardware pool to remove routing/fallback variance. capture per-request batch size and kernel-path header.
maya: agree. also add a temporary console panel for "batch-size distribution" and "kernel-path tag" by cohort+variant.
cheng: kernel_path is in trace metadata. i'll wire up a temporary panel and a routing-log filter for cohort shadow-A.
hailey: i'll run a synthetic eval (300 short requests, seq len 10-50) to both variants from the same client after the panel exists and capture cache-hit headers.
liam: note: autoscaler joined nodes around 14:03 per logs; midwindow node joins can change batching semantics and temporarily inflate p95.
maya: ops-bot can you confirm autoscale around 14:00-14:05?
ops-bot: autoscaler-bot: scale-event pool=gpu-pool-3 old=6 new=8 at 2025-03-05T14:03:05Z reason=CPU_pressure
cheng: autoscale happened, so some requests saw a mixing of old and new node batching behaviors.
maya: action items: cheng add panel + routing filter; liam run pinned A/B with kernel debug headers; hailey run synthetic eval; maya will collect results and add a short alert rule if v2 p95 > v1 p95 by 50% for 10m.
liam: i added a small harness script: `infra/smoke-tests/run_small_latency_check.sh --variant base-v2 --emit kernel-path`
hailey: tagging @product for rollout UX implications. large deltas will surface to tenants and may need to pause rollout.
product-bot: product-notify: prod-eng: investigation underway on variant p95 delta; may affect rollout cadence for v2.
maya: thanks. i'll post results here when we have the A/B + eval output. :thumbsup:
